chunks: And from him, from al-Nadr, from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abu Waddad Hafsh ibn Salim, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the greeting (salam) in the two rak'ahs of the Witr prayer, so he said: 'Yes. If you have a need, go out and fulfill it, then return and bow in one rak'ah.'

key_terms.التَّسْلِيمُ: The act of saying 'Assalamu Alaikum' to conclude or break the prayer
key_terms.الْوَتْرِ: The odd-numbered night prayer, typically performed after Isha

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on breaking the Witr prayer to attend to a need?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the flexibility of the Witr prayer structure, permitting the *taslim* (greeting) after the first two rak'ahs to allow for a brief interruption. This ruling highlights the practical jurisprudence of Shia prayer, where the Witr is treated as a flexible unit that can be paused for worldly needs and resumed with a single concluding rak'ah, emphasizing ease (*yusr*) in worship.
